$comment: Fork-delta registry for njuptlzf/pi-hermes-memory (fork of chandra447/pi-hermes-memory). Read by scripts/upstream-divergence.mjs (`npm run upstream:check`). status=planned means we intend to diverge but have not yet; status=applied means we already do — the check fails if an `applied` entry stops diverging (upstream absorbed it, or the change was lost). baseBlob pins the upstream file at the baseline ref so the check can warn when upstream moves under us.

entries.change: AGENT_ROOT splits into storageRoot (per scope, injected) and runtimeRoot (global, for pi module discovery); resolveAgentRoot stays as the runtime-root default
entries.reason: The whole point of the fork: one directory per (user, sub-scope), chosen by the host.

entries.change: adds defaultMemoryConfig() — a pure copy of the built-in defaults, no file/env read — so a host that owns configuration (an in-process multi-tenant server) never calls loadConfig(); the root itself is not threaded yet
entries.reason: loadConfig() resolves a JSON file under the agent root, which is one tenant's file becoming every tenant's config. 2 of the 27 AGENT_ROOT references still to thread.

entries.change: adds closeHandle() — close this coordinator's pinned connection only, next to the existing process-wide closeHandles()
entries.reason: Per-tenant erasure: Windows refuses to remove the tenant directory while .pi-hermes-locks.sqlite is open, and closeHandles() would drop every other tenant's connection to erase one.

entries.change: pure root algebra: storageRoot vs runtimeRoot, absolute-only validation, isInsideRoot() for erasure safety
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. No env, no homedir — the host computes both roots.

entries.change: createScopedHermesMemory({storageRoot}) → (pi) => handle; store + memory tool + policy prompt, no commands, no child_process, no env
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. The composition an in-process multi-tenant host can load.

entries.change: 7 cases: two tenants isolated in one process, duplicate-root refusal, erasure after dispose, root validation
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. The isolation invariant needs a test, not a comment.

entries.change: wrap the existing default export in an option-taking factory, e.g. createScopedHermesMemory({ storageRoot })
entries.reason: Entry is already a per-run factory; wrapping from outside keeps upstream's function body intact (avoids the same-function-body conflict class).

entries.change: SESSIONS_DIR (import-time constant, line 14) becomes lazy / parameter-supplied
entries.reason: 1 of the 2 import-time constants; must not resolve at import time or the fork cannot honour a per-run root.

entries.change: DEFAULT_SESSIONS_DIR (import-time constant, line 30) becomes lazy / parameter-supplied
entries.reason: The second import-time constant; already has an options.sessionsDir override to hook into.

entries.change: storage root threaded in instead of read from AGENT_ROOT
entries.reason: Bypasses config today; 2 references.

entries.change: lock directory derived from the injected root, never from a process-global
entries.reason: Two scopes in one process must not share a consolidation lock; a global setter would also cross directories under concurrency.

entries.change: root parameter instead of AGENT_ROOT
entries.reason: 4 references, the densest consumer after paths.ts.

entries.change: keep runtime module-discovery root on the global AGENT_ROOT (line 239); only memory storage follows the scope
entries.reason: Dual-root hazard: scoping this root would break pi module discovery for every session.

entries.change: root parameter instead of AGENT_ROOT
entries.reason: 1 reference; single-line surface.

entries.change: buildMemoryTargetRoutingGuidance() (line 230) rewritten to scope-relative wording instead of user/memory/failure global targets
entries.reason: This one function is what teaches the model to write outside the scope; it is the only prompt-side change needed.

entries.change: adds upstream:check scripts, a build script (tsc -p tsconfig.json), the scoped package name (@njuptlzf/pi-hermes-memory) and conditional exports (agent-chat-source -> src, default -> dist)
entries.reason: The gate needs an entry point; scripts-only edits merge trivially.

entries.change: surface map with per-row upstream call-site evidence
entries.reason: Fork-owned file; never conflicts on merge.

entries.change: measured v0.11.0 test baseline and the definition of green
entries.reason: Fork-owned file; never conflicts on merge.

entries.reason: Fork-owned file; never conflicts on merge.

entries.reason: Fork-owned file; never conflicts on merge.

entries.reason: Fork-owned file; upstream CI does not know this path.

entries.change: host-neutral provider descriptor: id/version/open, selfInjects=false; the module a host loads from configuration
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. This is the npm-facing entry for external registration: a host imports it by package specifier and never links against the fork build.

entries.change: 4 cases: id/version drift vs package.json, host-owned prompt, tool mount + single-tenant erasure, root validation
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. Version drift between package.json and the descriptor is exactly how a host ends up reporting the wrong engine version.

entries.change: capability-aware policy prompt: every sentence is true of the assembly that emits it (no global layer, no project target, no unmounted tool)
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. Upstream policy text is written for a single-user CLI; in a tenant it advertised a project target with no store and a memory_search tool that is not mounted.

entries.change: target-routed MemoryStore facade: user -> shared profile store, memory/failure -> scope store, unknown method throws
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. Keeps the engine untouched (zero hunks in memory-tool.ts) while giving user-writes a second home.

entries.change: 9 cases: cross-scope visibility, scope isolation, write routing, erasure split, root overlap refusal, policy truthfulness
entries.reason: Fork-owned file. The shared layer is where an erasure bug becomes a compliance bug.

entries.change: registry existence check names @njuptlzf/pi-hermes-memory instead of upstream pi-hermes-memory
entries.reason: The check decides whether a re-run publishes; pointing it at the wrong name makes every re-run look like a first publish.

entries.change: same registry check, same scoped name
entries.reason: Same reason as publish.yml.

entries.change: scoped name in trust commands, install lines and the fork note about per-package trusted publishing
entries.reason: A trust config created for upstream does nothing for this package.

entries.change: install command uses the scoped name; a banner states this is a fork
entries.reason: Installing the unscoped name gets upstream, not this fork.
